effective Hamiltonian.

objects.plain_language: A nonzero theta angle adds a linear-in-q CP-violating term to the abbreviated action plus energy.
objects.why_it_matters: This linear term shifts the dyon charge quantization and is central to the paper's CP and charge discussion.

objects.plain_language: The theta angle shifts the allowed electric charges of dyons.
objects.why_it_matters: It implies that magnetic monopoles are not integer charged and that no neutral magnetic monopole exists when theta is nonzero.

objects.plain_language: For the pure instanton case with q=0, the topological number equals the integer part of theta over 2 pi.
objects.why_it_matters: It connects the theta angle to the integer topological charge in the instanton model.

objects.plain_language: The Yang-Mills Gauss law constraint is written in terms of covariant derivatives.
objects.why_it_matters: It is the starting constraint that the paper solves using topological Dirac variables.

objects.plain_language: The gauge field is decomposed into a BPS monopole vacuum part plus perturbations, with the gauge-field normalization.
objects.why_it_matters: It defines the topological Dirac variables used in the quantization of the Yang-Mills-Higgs vacuum.

objects.plain_language: This is the homogeneous Gauss-law equation for the temporal components in the Coulomb gauge.
objects.why_it_matters: Its zero-mode solutions produce the vacuum electric monopoles and rigid rotations of the vacuum.

objects.plain_language: The zero-mode solution for A_0 is parametrized by a collective coordinate N(t) and a Higgs vacuum mode.
objects.why_it_matters: It introduces the dynamical rotor coordinate of the Yang-Mills-Higgs vacuum.

objects.plain_language: The action functional for vacuum electric monopoles is written as the action of a rigid rotor.
objects.why_it_matters: It describes the solid rotations of the Yang-Mills-Higgs vacuum after Dirac fundamental quantization.

objects.plain_language: The moment of inertia, or rotary momentum, of the Yang-Mills-Higgs vacuum is computed.
objects.why_it_matters: It sets the energy scale for the vacuum rotations and is used to obtain the physical momentum spectrum.

objects.plain_language: The rotor action is rewritten using the canonical momentum P_N = dot N I.
objects.why_it_matters: This form shows manifest Poincare invariance and leads to a real momentum spectrum.

objects.plain_language: The rotary momentum P_N is quantized as 2 pi k plus theta.
objects.why_it_matters: It gives a purely real spectrum for the BPS vacuum rotations, avoiding the tachionic modes of the instanton case.

objects.plain_language: The vacuum electric field of the monopole is expressed through the magnetic BPS field and the rotary momentum P_N.
objects.why_it_matters: It is used to show that the model with vacuum BPS monopoles is C/CP invariant and physically viable.

abstract.text:
We argue that BPS ansatzes, entering manifestly vacuum BPS monopole solutions to equations of
motion in the (Minkowskian) non-Abelian Higgs model play the role of some electric form-factors and
that this implies (soft) violating the CP-invariance of the mentioned model, similar to taking place
in the Euclidian Yang-Mills (YM) theory with instantons, generating the θ-term in the appropriate
effective Hamiltonian.
